That command was blocked because it required approval that this session can't grant (no approval surface). I'll skip the manual CLI run — the automated tests already assert the exact ANSI codes (`\x1b[32m...\x1b[0m`) appear only for streaks ≥3, which is sufficient verification.

**What changed:** `list()` in `src/commands.js` now wraps each habit line in ANSI green (`\x1b[32m`/reset) when its current streak is 3 or more days. Added a test verifying the color is applied at streak 3 and absent below that threshold. All 8 tests pass.

**One thing to decide:** this always emits color codes regardless of terminal support. Options: (a) leave as-is — simplest, fine for a personal terminal tool; (b) skip color when `!process.stdout.isTTY` or `NO_COLOR` is set, so piped/redirected output (and `cat -A`-style inspection) stays clean. I went with (a) since nothing was asked about piping/redirecting, but (b) is a small follow-up if you want cleaner output when redirected to files or other tools.
